text: קניתי iPhone חדש בחנות ליד הבית.
note: English word mid-sentence: iPhone reads LTR in place, the period stays at the far left.
English at the end followed by a period: the period must stay at the end of the Hebrew sentence.
English at the start: the paragraph stays RTL (book default) although the first strong letter is Latin.
Digits read LTR and stay in place in the sentence.
Paragraph opens with digits: digits are weak, the first strong letter is Hebrew.
Number range with an en dash.
Minus sign: can show as 5- without an LRM (the 4.2 escape hatch).
Phone number stays together LTR.
Time stays together LTR.
Date with dots stays together LTR.
Shekel sign before the number.
Dollar sign before the number.
Price followed by a Hebrew abbreviation with gershayim.

text: הסבר נוסף מופיע בהמשך (ראה Chapter 3) ובנספח.
note: Parentheses are mirrored characters and must show correctly in RTL.
English sentence with punctuation inside Hebrew: one LTR run, the exclamation mark stays with world.

text: It was a quiet morning, and nobody on the street had yet heard the news.
note: A whole English paragraph inside the Hebrew book: carries dir=ltr, aligns left.

text: שלום, קוראים לי דנה, והיא ענתה בשקט.
note: A Hebrew paragraph inside an English book: carries dir=rtl.

text: האתר נמצא בכתובת https://example.com/books ויש בו הכול.
note: URL inside Hebrew text.
Email address inside Hebrew text.
Percentage.
Gershayim U+05F4 in an acronym: punctuation, not a letter.
Geresh U+05F3 in a loanword.
Hebrew letter numerals with gershayim.
Vowel points are combining marks, never strong.
Points before the first letter must not decide the direction.
Maqaf U+05BE joins words and is punctuation.
A line of poetry.
